idiom_name: Spring @Service class with primary-constructor injection and @Transactional
implementation_notes: Kotlin keeps the Spring service class but removes the ceremony: dependencies are primary-constructor val parameters, and the kotlin-spring (all-open) plugin opens @Service/@Transactional classes and their members so proxy-based interception can subclass them. Declarative @Transactional works on ordinary blocking methods; for suspend functions and Flow the transaction must be programmatic (TransactionalOperator.executeAndAwait, Flow.transactional) because a thread-bound transaction manager does not follow a suspension point. The classic hand-wired service (a plain class in a module, constructed from main or a test) is still the simpler choice for applications that do not run a container at all.
pitfalls: Without the kotlin-spring plugin, final classes and members cannot be proxied and @Transactional silently does nothing.
A suspend function under thread-bound @Transactional leaves the transaction behind at the first suspension; use executeAndAwait or TransactionalOperator.
Mixing blocking JDBC calls with coroutines in the same service starves the dispatcher - pick one model per layer or offload explicitly.
